newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs easier on profit taking, bellies strong.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs easier on profit taking, bellies strong.

text.p: CME hog futures were mostly lower at midsession on profit taking after new highs were set, and pork bellies remained strong despite a wave of profit taking early after new highs in that pit were posted, traders said.

At 1126 CDT, hog futures were off 0.450 cent per lb to up 0.150 cent with June off most at 85.000 cents after setting a new contract high early at 85.700 cents. July also posted a new high of 85.300 before falling. Pork belly futures posted gains of 0.850 to 3.000 cents with thinly traded March '98 up the limit. May was up the least at 88.400 cents after setting a new high of 89.400. All pork belly months set new highs.

Hog futures briefly posted gains but were pressured by profit taking and speculative selling. Futures were seen approaching a near term top, especially after record volume for new lean contracts was set Thursday.
A sharp spike in volume usually indicates a top or bottom in the market. Recent gains in cash pork products may also turn off domestic demand, traders said.
But support in deferred months remained, linked to expectations global demand for U.S. pork will be strong this year because of bans on Taiwan and Netherlands pork.

Rand Financials and Lind-Waldock sold June while RBH sold July, traders said, and Cargill Investor Services was on both sides of the market. ABN Chicogo Corp and Smith Barney bought August and October.
In hog options commission houses were offering 86 and higher June calls and buying 82 puts, pit sources said.

Concern that high pork prices would weigh on domestic demand added to a round of profit taking in pork bellies after values in that pit posted new contract highs in all months. But futures again surged for gains after filling a gap left in charts at the opening. Bullish expectations on the monthly Cold Storage report also kept bellies supported, traders said.
Analyst expectations on the amount of bellies in U.S. warehouses as of April 1 in USDA's report ranged from 49 million to 53.2 million lbs versus 47.655 million on hand last year.

The report would have to show storings above the high end of expectations to be remotely considered bearish as there has been little product moving into storage during April, traders said. Stocks could easily slip below year-ago levels during April which would be very bullish for prices going into the peak summer demand season, traders said.
A recent light hog slaughter pace and news that Japan was buying U.S. pork bellies added to bullish ideas.
USDA estimated week-to-date hog slaughter through Thursday at 349,000 head, above 341,000 in the same period last week but well below 363,000 in the year-ago period.
Cash bellies climbed to best levels since early October and hog kills are running four percent under projections from the last Hogs and Pigs report, analysts noted.

Prudential Securities notably bought at the start before selling by Rand Financials and R.J. O'Brien took prices down below previous levels, traders said. General demand then boosted the market going into midsession, pit sources said.
